answer: Rewards settle per cluster, not per key. The ledger groups identities sharing attestors, funding or timing into one cluster, and a cluster draws one share of the epoch pool however many keys it holds; that share is divided among the members. Ten aliases on one knoll split a single worker's payout while paying ten escrows and answering ten audits, so cost per unit of reward climbs with the square of the headcount. Honest arrivals keep a separate pulse and a separate share, and the onyx record of past groupings is permanent, so regrouping cannot restore the weight already lost.
